extracted text: The study examines three Al-Mg-Zn alloys with varying Mg content (2-4 wt%) and approximately 5.25 wt% Zn. The materials were prepared as book-mold castings, homogenized at 550°C for approximately 8 hours, hot-and-warm rolled at temperatures from 450 to 350°C, and then cold rolled to a thickness of 4.1 mm. Tension test results are available for two aging conditions: NAN (30 min, 840 h) which represents simulated paint-bake aging followed by natural aging, and NA (500 min) which represents peak-aged condition. The alloys show yield strengths from 192-249 MPa for NAN condition and 340-412 MPa for NA condition, with UTS values ranging from 320-401 MPa for NAN condition and 381-462 MPa for NA condition. Elongation to failure was approximately 17% for NAN condition and 8-17% for NA condition.
property mapping:
YS = Yield strength (MPa)
UTS = Ultimate tensile strength (MPa)
EF = Elongation to failure (%)
VHN = Vickers hardness number
K = Strength coefficient (MPa)
n = Strain-hardening exponent
abbreviations:
N(x) = Natural aging: Solutionized at 450°C for 30 min, water quenched, then naturally aged at 25°C for x hours
A(x) = Artificial aging: Solutionized at 450°C for 30 min, water quenched, then artificially aged at 175°C for x minutes
NA(x) = Natural/artificial aging: Solutionized at 450°C for 30 min, water quenched, naturally aged at 25°C for 168 or 240 hours, then artificially aged at 175°C for x minutes
NAN(x,y) = Natural/artificial/natural aging: Solutionized at 450°C for 30 min, water quenched, naturally aged at 25°C for 168 or 240 hours, artificially aged at 175°C for x minutes, air cooled, and naturally aged at 25°C for y hours
